newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kookmin seeks higher foreign ownership.
newsitem.headline: Kookmin seeks higher foreign ownership.

text.p: South Korea's Kookmin Bank said on Monday it has asked the Securities Supervisory Board to allow foreign investors to buy an additional 4.5 percent of its share capital above the new foreign shareholding limit of 23 percent.

A Kookmin official said the increase was needed because there were no available shares for foreign investors since the bank issued $300 million in depository receipts last September, 13.86 percent of its share capital.
Foreign investors currently hold 15.5 percent of Kookmin Bank shares.
South Korea will raise the foreign stock holding limit to 23 percent on Friday from 20 percent at present.
The law allows Kookmin to exempt the additional 4.5 percent it is seeking to sell to foreigners from the ceiling.
If the bank's request is approved, another 4.18 million Kookmin shares would be made available to foreign investors.
